commits.message:
feat(core): a cell carries where its owner drew it, so a nested widget's position is read off the frame (rich-runtime-fna.1)

The design answer for the composed runtime, landed as its contract rather
than a design document, as rich-viewport-owi.1 did. An origin threaded down
the render options cannot exist: Align places each line after rendering it,
so one widget's rows start at different columns. Position travels up
instead: `Anchor` rides on each segment's Style, which every container
already preserves, and `Segment.anchorAt` reads any cell of a composed
frame. test/core/anchor.test.ts proves it through every container.

The remaining answers are on rich-runtime-fna.2, .3, .4 and
rich-viewport-owi.5.

refactor(examples): every scrolling pane is a Viewport; the hand-rolled clipping is gone (rich-viewport-owi.6) (#190)

* refactor(examples): every scrolling pane is a Viewport; the hand-rolled clipping is gone (rich-viewport-owi.6)

`examples/shared/window.ts`, its rich-explore re-export, and the inline
clip-and-centre code in the claude-sessions viewer and global-results panes
are deleted. The tree, sidebar, viewer, results and preview panes each keep
one Viewport across frames and follow the selection with `ensureVisible`.

Behaviour changes worth knowing:
- The selection is kept in view by the least scroll, not centred.
- claude-sessions draws through Live's alt screen, which hands the frame
  an exact region; its panes no longer compute their own heights.
- rich-explore's preview scroll lives in its viewport, not AppState; `G`
  stops at the last full view instead of scrolling into blank rows.
- The claude-sessions browser/viewer split is now `ratio` 1:3, which shows
  Layout's dropped-remainder row (rich-layout-xvv).

* fix(examples): review pass — roots stay reachable, panes open per subject, items count at the viewport's width (rich-viewport-owi.6)

- Tree and sidebar keep a line either side of the selection in view, so
  the root comes back above the first entry once a pane has scrolled.
- Viewport.contentWidth names the width its content renders at; render
  and measure use it, and ItemsInView counts lines at it, so a scrollbar
  no longer desyncs the selection range from the lines shown.
- ViewportPerSubject (examples/shared) replaces rich-explore's inline
  previewOf and gives claude-sessions' viewer and results a viewport per
  session and per query, instead of inheriting the last one's scroll.
- The first frame renders inside the promise whose cleanup restores the
  terminal, so a throw there no longer strands raw mode and the alt screen.
